Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 97, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 4):

Tafsir of Surat al-Qadr [In A: "Surat Laylat al-Qadr".]
It is Meccan.
In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
* *
Allah, exalted is He, informs that He sent down the Qur'an on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), which is the blessed night about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 3], and it is the Night of Power, and it is in the month of Ramadan, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].
Ibn 'Abbas and others said: Allah sent the Qur'an down all at once from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the House of Glory (Bayt al-'Izza) in the lowest heaven, and then it was sent down in parts, according to events, over twenty-three years upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then He, exalted is He, said, magnifying the status of the Night of Power, in which He singled out the sending down of the Great Qur'an: ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾.
Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi, when commenting on this verse, said: Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Abu Dawud at-Tayalisi narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Hudani [In A: "al-Judhami".] narrated to us from Yusuf ibn Sa'd, who said: A man stood up before al-Hasan ibn 'Ali after he had pledged allegiance to Mu'awiyah and said: "You have blackened the faces of the believers" – or: "O you who blacken the faces of the believers" – so he said: "Do not reproach me, may Allah have mercy on you; the Prophet ﷺ was shown the Banu Umayyah on his pulpit, and that grieved him, so there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ – O Muhammad – meaning a river in Paradise – and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power. And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – the Banu Umayyah will rule it after you, O Muhammad." Al-Qasim said: "We counted, and it came to a thousand months, not exceeding a day or falling short by a day." [Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3350).]
Then at-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith, which we only know from this route, through the hadith of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, and he is trustworthy; Yahya al-Qattan and Ibn Mahdi declared him trustworthy. He said: His teacher Yusuf ibn Sa'd – and it is said: Yusuf ibn Mazin – is an unknown man, and we do not know this hadith in this wording except through this route.
This hadith was also narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, from Yusuf ibn Mazin, with the same [Al-Mustadrak (3/170), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il an-Nubuwwah (6/509).] . Al-Tirmidhi's statement that this Yusuf is unknown is open to question, for a group narrated from him, among them Hammad ibn Salamah, Khalid al-Hadhdha', and Yunus ibn 'Ubayd. Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "He is well known," and in a report from Ibn Ma'in [he said]: "He is trustworthy." [Addition from M.] Ibn Jarir narrated it through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, from 'Isa ibn Mazin, so he said, and this implies confusion (idtirab) in this hadith, and Allah knows best. Then this hadith, in every case, is extremely munkar (rejected). Our shaykh, the Imam, the Hafiz, the Proof Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: "It is a munkar hadith."
I say: The statement of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Hudani [In A: "al-Judhami".] that he calculated the period of the Banu Umayyah and found it to be a thousand months, not exceeding a day or falling short by a day, is not correct. Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him, became sole ruler when al-Hasan ibn 'Ali handed over the command to him in the year forty (AH), and the allegiance was unified for Mu'awiyah, and that year was called the Year of Unity (ʿAm al-Jama'a). Then they continued in it consecutively in al-Sham and elsewhere; it was not taken from them except during the rule of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr in the two Sanctuaries, al-Ahwaz and some regions, for nearly nine years, but their hand was not wholly removed from command, only from some regions, until the 'Abbasids seized the caliphate from them in the year one hundred and thirty-two (AH). So the total of their period is ninety-two years, and that is more than a thousand months, for a thousand months is equivalent to eighty-three years and four months. It seems al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl dropped from their period the days of Ibn al-Zubayr, and on this basis what he said is close to correct in calculation, and Allah knows best.
Among what indicates the weakness of this hadith is that it is framed to disparage the rule of the Banu Umayyah, and if that were intended it would not have been in this context; for the excellence of the Night of Power over their days does not indicate the blame of their days, since the Night of Power is very noble, and the noble surah came only to praise the Night of Power. How then would it be praised by being preferred over the days of the Banu Umayyah, which, by the implication of this hadith, are blameworthy? Is this not like what the poet said:
Do you not see that the sword's worth diminishes
when it is said that the sword is more effective than the staff?
And another said:
When you prefer a man of skill
over one deficient, the praise becomes a deficiency.
Then what is understood from the Qur'an's reference to the thousand months mentioned in the verse [In M: "Then what is understood from the verse that".] is the days of the Banu Umayyah, while the surah is Meccan, so how can it refer to a thousand months being the rule of the Banu Umayyah, when neither the wording nor the meaning of the verse indicates it?! The pulpit was made in Madinah only after a period from the Hijrah. All of this indicates the weakness and rejection of this hadith, and Allah knows best. [And see: al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (6/243, 244), for he also expanded on the discussion of this hadith.]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muslim – meaning Ibn Khalid – informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who wore weapons in the path of Allah for a thousand months. He said: The Muslims marvelled at that. He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power. And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – the night in which that man wore weapons in the path of Allah for a thousand months. [Al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, as in the takhrij of al-Zayla'i's Takhrij al-Kashshaf (4/253), narrated it through the route of Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with it as a mursal report.]
Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Mujahid, who said: There was a man among the Children of Israel who would stand in prayer at night until morning, then strive against the enemy by day until evening, and he did this for a thousand months, so Allah revealed this verse: ﴿The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – the standing in prayer on that night is better than that man's deeds. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/167).]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Maslamah ibn 'Ali narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn 'Urwah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once mentioned four men from the Children of Israel who worshipped Allah for eighty years without disobeying Him for the blink of an eye: he mentioned Ayyub, Zakariyya, Hizqil ibn al-'Ajuz, and Yusha' ibn Nun. He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marvelled at that, so Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, your Ummah marvels at the worship of these men for eighty years without disobeying Him for the blink of an eye; Allah has sent down something better than that." Then he recited to him: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power. And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – this is better than what you and your Ummah marvelled at. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delighted by that, and so were the people with him. [And al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/569) and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim.]
Sufyan al-Thawri said: It reached me from Mujahid: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." He said: Its deeds – its fasting and its standing in prayer – are better than a thousand months. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months" – the Night of Power is not among those months. Qatadah ibn Di'amah, al-Shafi'i, and others besides them said likewise.
'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i said: Deeds performed in it are better than the deeds of a thousand months.
This view, that it is better than worship of a thousand months – and that the Night of Power is not among them – is the choice of Ibn Jarir. It is the correct view and not what differs from it, and it is like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "A night of guarding (ribat) in the path of Allah is better than a thousand nights elsewhere in other stations." Narrated by Ahmad [Al-Musnad (1/62), from the hadith of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him.] And like what has come concerning one who goes to the Friday prayer with good bearing and a good intention: "It is written for him the reward of a year's deeds, the reward of its fasting and its standing in prayer," and other meanings similar to these.
Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When Ramadan arrived, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The month of Ramadan has come to you, a blessed month. Allah has made its fasting obligatory upon you. The gates of Paradise are opened in it, the gates of Hellfire are closed in it, and the devils are chained in it. In it is a night better than a thousand months; whoever is deprived of its good has indeed been deprived."
An-Nasa'i also narrated it through the hadith of Ayyub, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (2/230) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (4/129).]
Since the worship on the Night of Power equals the worship of a thousand months, it is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Power in faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1901) and Sahih Muslim no. (760).]
* *
His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ means: the angels descend in abundance on this night because of the abundance of its blessing, and the angels descend along with the descent of blessing and mercy, just as they descend at the recitation of the Qur'an, surround the circles of remembrance, and lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge out of sincere reverence for him.
As for the Spirit, it has been said that what is meant here is Jibril, peace be upon him, so it is of the type of mentioning the specific after the general. It has also been said that they are a kind of angel, as was mentioned earlier in Surat an-Naba'. And Allah knows best.
* *
His saying: ﴿concerning every matter﴾ – Mujahid said: "Peace is it, concerning every matter."
Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Peace is it﴾, he said: "It is safe; Satan cannot do any evil in it or cause any harm in it."
Qatadah and others said: Matters are decided therein, and lifespans and provisions are determined, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Therein every wise matter is distinguished﴾.
* *
His saying: ﴿Peace it is until the rising of the dawn﴾. Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿concerning every matter, peace it is until the rising of the dawn﴾, he said: "It is the greeting of the angels on the Night of Power to the people of the mosques, until dawn rises."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: "Min kulli imri'in salamun hiya hatta matli'i al-fajr" (from every person, peace it is until the rising of the dawn).

Al-Bayhaqi, in his book Fada'il al-Awqat, narrated from 'Ali a strange report about the descent of the angels, their passing by those who pray on the Night of Power, and the attainment of blessing by those who pray.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar a very strange and wondrous, extremely lengthy report about the descent of the angels from Sidrat al-Muntaha in the company of Jibril, peace be upon him, to the earth, and their supplication for the believing men and women. [The report will be cited at the explanation of the end of the surah.]

Ibn Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Imran (i.e., al-Qattan) narrated to us from Qatadah, from Abu Maymunah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the Night of Decree: "It is a night of the twenty-seventh or the twenty-ninth, and the angels on that night on the earth are more numerous than the pebbles" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2545).]].

al-A'mash said, from al-Minhal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, regarding His words ﴿Peace it is, until the emergence of dawn﴾: "No matter is decreed in it."

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿Peace it is﴾, meaning: "It is entirely good; there is no evil in it until the rising of dawn." This meaning is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Haywah [[In A: "Abdah".]] ibn Shurayh narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us: Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Night of Decree is in the last ten nights. Whoever stands in prayer during them, seeking its reward, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sins and what followed. It is an odd night: the ninth, the seventh, the fifth, the third, or the last night." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: "The sign of the Night of Decree is that it is clear and bright, as if there were a shining moon in it, still and calm, neither cold nor hot, and no shooting star is permitted to be thrown on that night until morning. Its sign is that the sun rises in the morning level, without rays like the moon on the night of the full moon, and the Shaytan is not permitted to come out with it that day" [[Al-Musnad (5/324).]].

This chain is good (hasan), but the text has strangeness (gharabah), and some of its wording is objectionable (nakarah).

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Zam'ah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding the Night of Decree: "It is a gentle, open night, neither hot nor cold, and the sun of its morning rises weak and red" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2680), in which it reads "safiqah" instead of "ḍa'ifah".]].

Ibn Abi Asim al-Nabil narrated with his chain from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw the Night of Decree and then I was made to forget it. It is in the last ten nights. Among its nights is a clear, bright night, neither hot nor cold, as if there were a moon in it. Its Shaytan does not come out until its dawn breaks" [[Al-Kanz (8/540), no. (24069), attributed it to him, but I have not found it in the Sunnah. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2190), through Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, in similar wording.]].

**Section**

The scholars differed: was the Night of Decree in earlier nations, or is it specific to this Ummah? There are two opinions.

Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri said: Malik narrated to us that it reached him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shown the lifespans of people before him, or what Allah willed of that, and it seemed that the lifespans of his Ummah were too short for them to reach the same amount of deeds that others reached in long life. So Allah gave him the Night of Decree, which is better than a thousand months [[Al-Muwatta' in the narration of al-Zuhri, no. (889).]]. It has also been traced through another chain.

What Malik said implies that this Ummah is specifically given the Night of Decree. The author of "al-Uddah," one of the imams of the Shafi'is, transmitted this from the majority of scholars, and Allah knows best. Al-Khattabi reported a consensus (ijma') on it, and al-Rafi'i stated it definitively as the position of the school (madhhab). What the hadith indicates is that it existed in the earlier nations as it does in our Ummah.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar: Abu Zumayl Simak al-Hanafi narrated to me: Malik ibn Murthid ibn Abd Allah narrated to me: Murthid narrated to me, saying: I asked Abu Dharr: "How did you ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Night of Decree?" He said: "I used to ask people about it. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me about the Night of Decree: is it in Ramadan or in another month?' He said: 'Rather, it is in Ramadan.' I said: 'Does it remain with the prophets as long as they are alive, and when they die it is lifted?' He said: 'Rather, it remains until the Day of Resurrection.' I said: 'In which Ramadan is it?' He said: 'Seek it in the first ten and the last ten.'" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke and kept talking, then I seized his moment of distraction and said: "In which of the two tens is it?" He said: "Seek it in the last ten nights; do not ask me about anything after that." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke again, then I seized his moment of distraction and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I adjure you by my right over you, tell me in which ten it is." He became angry with me with an anger the like of which he had not shown since I accompanied him, and said: "Seek it in the last seven nights; do not ask me about anything after that."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from al-Fallas, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/171) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (3427).]].

In it is evidence for what we mentioned, and in it is that it continues until the Day of Resurrection, every year [after the Prophet ﷺ] [[Addition from A.]]. This is not as some sects of the Shi'ah claimed, that it was lifted entirely, based on their understanding of the hadith we will mention below, in his words, peace be upon him: "It was lifted, and perhaps that is better for you," because what is meant is the lifting of knowledge of its exact time. It also indicates that the Night of Decree is specifically tied to the month of Ramadan among all other months, not as was reported from Ibn Mas'ud and those who followed him among the scholars of Kufa, that it can be found in all of the year and is hoped for equally in all months.

Abu Dawud in his Sunan titled a chapter on this: "Chapter on clarifying that the Night of Decree is in every Ramadan." He narrated: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh al-Nasa'i [[In M: "al-Shami".]] informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us: Musa ibn Uqbah narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, while I was listening, about the Night of Decree, and he said: "It is in every Ramadan" [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1387).]].

This chain's narrators are trustworthy (thiqah), except that Abu Dawud said: Shu'bah and Sufyan narrated it from Abu Ishaq, and they stopped it (at Ibn Umar, as a statement, not a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ).

It has been reported from Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, a narration that it is hoped for throughout the whole month of Ramadan. This is an opinion (wajh) transmitted by al-Ghazali, and al-Rafi'i considered it very strange.

**Section**

Then it has been said: it is on the first night of the month of Ramadan, reported from Abu Razin. It has also been said: it falls on the night of the seventeenth. Abu Dawud narrated a hadith on this from Ibn Mas'ud, traced to the Prophet ﷺ, and it is also reported as a statement (mawquf) attributed to him, and to Zayd ibn Arqam and Uthman ibn Abi al-As.

This is an opinion from Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, and it is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri. They justified it by saying that it is the night of Badr. It was a Friday night, the seventeenth of Ramadan, and in its morning was the Battle of Badr, the day of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿the Day of Criterion﴾ [Al-Anfal: 41].

It has been said: the nineteenth night, reported also from Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both.

It has been said: the twenty-first night, based on the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ secluded himself (i'tikaf) in the first ten days of Ramadan, and we secluded ourselves with him. Then Jibril came to him and said: "What you seek is ahead of you." So he secluded himself in the middle ten, and we secluded ourselves with him. Then Jibril came to him and said: "[What] you seek is ahead of you [[Addition from M and A.]]." Then the Prophet ﷺ stood up delivering a sermon on the morning of the twentieth of Ramadan, and said: "Whoever was secluded with me should return, for I was shown the Night of Decree, and I was made to forget it. It is in the last ten nights, in odd nights. I saw myself prostrating in mud and water." The roof of the mosque was made of palm fronds, and we did not see anything in the sky, but then a cloud came and it rained, and the Prophet ﷺ led us in prayer until I saw the trace of mud and water on the forehead of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, confirming his vision. In another wording: "In the morning of the twenty-first." They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1167).]].

al-Shafi'i said: This hadith is the most authentic of the reports.

It has been said: the twenty-third night, based on the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Unays in Sahih Muslim [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1168).]], which is close in context to the narration of Abu Sa'id. Allah knows best.

It has been said: the twenty-fourth night. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-fourth." Its chain's narrators are trustworthy [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2167).]].

Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from al-Sunabihi, from Bilal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-fourth" [[Al-Musnad (6/12).]].

Ibn Lahi'ah is weak (da'if). What contradicts him is what al-Bukhari narrated from Asbagh, from Ibn Wahb, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Abu Abd Allah al-Sunabihi, who said: Bilal, the muezzin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, informed me that it is the first of the seven nights of the last ten. So this statement traced to a companion is more authentic, and Allah knows best. Similarly it has been reported from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abd Allah ibn Wahb that it is the night of the twenty-fourth. It has already been mentioned in the commentary of Surah al-Baqarah [[At the commentary of verse 185.]] the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' traced to the Prophet ﷺ: "The Qur'an was sent down on the night of the twenty-fourth."

It has been said: it is the night of the twenty-fifth, based on what al-Bukhari narrated from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek it in the last ten nights of Ramadan, on the ninth remaining, on the seventh remaining, on the fifth remaining." Many scholars interpreted this as the odd nights, which is more apparent and more well-known. Others understood it as the even nights, as narrated by Muslim from Abu Sa'id, who interpreted it that way. Allah knows best.

It has been said: it is the night of the twenty-seventh, based on what Muslim narrated in his Sahih from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "It is the night of the twenty-seventh."

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us: I heard Abdah and Asim, from Zirr: I asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b, "Abu al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Mas'ud says: 'Whoever stands in prayer throughout the year will find the Night of Decree.'" He said: "May Allah have mercy on him. He knew that it is in the month of Ramadan, and that it is the night of the twenty-seventh." Then he swore an oath. I said: "How do you know that?" He said: "By the sign, or the verse, that he told us of: the sun rises on that day without rays." Referring to the sun [[Al-Musnad (5/130).]].

And Muslim narrated it through the chains of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, Shu'ba and al-Awza'i, from 'Abda, from Zirr, from Ubayy, and he mentioned it, and in it he said: "By Allah, other than whom there is no god, it is in Ramadan," (he swore without making an exception), "By Allah, I know which night is the Night of Decree, the one the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to stand in prayer during. It is the night of the twenty-seventh, and its sign is that the sun rises on its morning white, without rays." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (762).]]

There are also reports on this from Mu'awiya, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas and others [[See these and other hadiths in al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti (8/570-580).]], from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that it is the night of the twenty-seventh. This is the view of a group of the early scholars (al-salaf), and it is the well-trodden path (al-jadda) of the school of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is also a narration from Abu Hanifa. It has been related from some of the early scholars that he tried to derive that it is the night of the twenty-seventh from the Qur'an, from the words ﴿It [is]﴾, because it is the twenty-seventh word of the surah. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari related to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada and 'Asim, that they both heard 'Ikrima say: Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab summoned the companions of Muhammad [[In A: "companions of the Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ and asked them about the Night of Decree, and they agreed that it is in the last ten nights. Ibn 'Abbas said: I said to 'Umar: "I know, or I think, which night of the Night of Decree it is." 'Umar said: "Which night is it?" [I said] [[Addition from M and A.]] "The seventh that passes, or the seventh that remains, of the last ten nights." 'Umar said: "How did you know that?" Ibn 'Abbas said: I said: "Allah created seven heavens, seven earths and seven days; the month revolves around seven; man was created from seven; he eats from seven; he prostrates on seven; the circumambulation of the House is seven; the stoning of the pillars is seven..." for things he mentioned. 'Umar said: "You have indeed understood a matter that we did not understand." Qatada would add to Ibn 'Abbas's statement "and he eats from seven" that it refers to the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then We caused to grow therein grain, and grapes and herbs [[Addition from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/322).]] ...﴾ [Abasa: 27, 28] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/322).]].

This is a good chain (isnad, the chain of narrators), strong, but its wording (matn) is very unusual.

It has also been said that it occurs on the night of the twenty-ninth. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, related to us, Sa'id ibn Salama related to us, 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil related to us, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Night of Decree, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Ramadan. So seek it in the last ten nights, for it is on an odd night: the twenty-first, or the twenty-third, or the twenty-fifth, or the twenty-seventh, [or the twenty-ninth] [[Addition from A and al-Musnad.]], or on the last night." [[Al-Musnad (5/321).]]

Al-Imam Ahmad also said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, that is Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, related to us, 'Imran al-Qattan related to us, from Qatada, from Abu Maymuna [[In A: "from Abu Mu'awiya".]], from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the Night of Decree: "It is the seventh or the ninth and twentieth night, and the angels on that night on the earth are more numerous than the number of pebbles." [[Al-Musnad (2/519).]]

Only Ahmad related this, and its chain is acceptable (la ba'sa bihi).

It has also been said that it occurs on the last night, due to what preceded in this hadith just now [[In A: "also".]], and due to what al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related, from the hadith of 'Uyayna ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Bakra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In the nine remaining, or the seven remaining, or the five remaining, or the three, or the last night." He meant: seek the Night of Decree. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (794) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (3404).]]

Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih. In the Musnad, through the chain of Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the Night of Decree: "It is the last night." [[I have not found it in the Musnad, but al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/572) and attributed it to Ahmad. Perhaps I will add it later.]]

Section

Al-Shafi'i [al-Imam] [[Addition from A.]] said regarding these narrations: They were issued by the Prophet ﷺ as an answer to the questioner, when it was said to him: "Shall I seek the Night of Decree on such-and-such night?" and he would say: "Yes." The Night of Decree is only a specific night that does not shift. This was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi from him in meaning. And it is related from Abu Qilaba that he said: "The Night of Decree shifts within the last ten nights."

What he related from Abu Qilaba was explicitly stated by Malik, al-Thawri, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu Thawr, al-Muzani, Abu Bakr ibn Khuzayma and others. It is also attributed to al-Shafi'i, as transmitted by al-Qadi from him, and it is the more likely view. And Allah knows best.

This view may find some support in what is established in the two Sahihs, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: that some men from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ were shown the Night of Decree in dreams in the last seven nights of Ramadan, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I see that your dreams agree on the last seven nights, so whoever seeks it, let him seek it in the last seven nights." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2015) and Sahih Muslim no. (1165).]]

Also in them, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek the Night of Decree on the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2017) and Sahih Muslim no. (1169). The wording is that of al-Bukhari.]]

Al-Shafi'i's position that it does not shift and is fixed within the month is argued from what al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to inform us of the Night of Decree, but two men among the Muslims quarrelled, and he said: "I went out to inform you of the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, so it was lifted. Perhaps that is better for you. So seek it on the ninth, the seventh and the fifth." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2023).]]

The point of evidence from it: if it were not fixed and continuously specified, they would not have come to know its specific night every year, since if it shifted they would only have known its specific night in that one year. Unless it is said that he went out only to inform them of it that year.

* *

His saying "so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, so it was lifted": in it there is support for what is said, that disputation cuts off benefit and beneficial knowledge, as came in the hadith: "Indeed a servant is deprived of provision through a sin that befalls him."

* *

His saying "it was lifted" means that the knowledge of its specific identity was lifted from you, not that it was lifted entirely from existence, as the ignorant among the Shi'a say, because he said after this: "So seek it on the ninth, the seventh and the fifth."

* *

His saying "Perhaps that is better for you" means: its not being specified for you, for when it is undetermined, those seeking it strive to find it in all the places where it is hoped for, and this produces more worship. This is unlike when they know its specific night, for then their resolve would be limited to standing in prayer on it alone. The wisdom required its being undetermined so that worship would encompass the whole month in seeking it, and the striving would be greater in the last ten nights. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) in the last ten nights of Ramadan until Allah took him, Mighty and Majestic is He. Then his wives observed i'tikaf after him. Both of them [al-Bukhari and Muslim] related it from the hadith of 'A'isha. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2026) and Sahih Muslim no. (1172).]]

And they both have from Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe i'tikaf in the last ten nights of Ramadan. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2025) and Sahih Muslim no. (1171).]]

'A'isha said: When the last ten nights began, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend the night in worship, wake his family, and tighten his waist-wrap (shadd al-mi'zar). Both of them related it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2024) and Sahih Muslim no. (1174).]]

Muslim has from her [[In M: "from both of them".]]: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would strive in the ten nights more than he strove at any other time. [[Sahih Muslim no. (1175).]]

This is the meaning of her words "and tightened the waist-wrap." It has been said that what is meant by it is abstaining from women. It may be that it is a metaphor for both matters, based on what Imam Ahmad related:

Suraij related to us, Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, who said: When ten nights of Ramadan remained, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would tighten his waist-wrap and withdraw from his wives. Ahmad alone related it. [[Al-Musnad (6/66).]]

It has been related from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, that all the nights of the last ten are equal in seeking the Night of Decree, and no one night is preferred over another. I saw this in the Sharh of al-Rafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

The recommended course is to increase supplication at all times, more in Ramadan, more in its last ten nights, and more on its odd nights. It is recommended to repeatedly say: "O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me," because of what Imam Ahmad related:

Yazid, that is Ibn Harun, related to us, al-Jurayri [[In M: "al-Jawhari".]], that is Sa'id ibn Iyas, related to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Buraida, that 'A'isha said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I happen to coincide with the Night of Decree, what should I supplicate?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me." [[Al-Musnad (6/182).]]

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Maja, through the chain of Kahmas ibn al-Hasan, from 'Abdullah ibn Buraida, from 'A'isha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if I know which night is the Night of Decree, what should I say in it?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3513), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11688) and Sunan Ibn Maja no. (3850).]]

This is the wording of al-Tirmidhi, then he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Hakim also related it in his Mustadrak and said: "This is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs." [[Al-Mustadrak (1/531).]] Al-Nasa'i also related it through the chain of Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Alqama ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraida, from 'A'isha, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if I coincide with the Night of Decree, what should I say in it?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10713).]]

A strange report and a wondrous account is mentioned, connected to the Night of Decree, which Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim related when interpreting this noble surah, and he said:

حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي زِيَادٍ الْقَطَوَانِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا سَيَّارُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، يَعْنِي الرَّاسِبِيَّ، عَنْ هِلَالٍ أَبِي جَبَلَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ السَّلَامِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ كَعْبٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: إِنَّ **Sidrat al-Muntaha** (سِدْرَةَ الْمُنْتَهَى، the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary) عَلَى حَدِّ السَّمَاءِ السَّابِعَةِ، مِمَّا يَلِي الْجَنَّةَ، فَهِيَ عَلَى حَدِّ هَوَاءِ الدُّنْيَا وَهَوَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ، عُلُوُّهَا فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَعُرُوقُهَا وَأَغْصَانُهَا مِنْ تَحْتِ الْكُرْسِيِّ [the Kursi], فِيهَا مَلَائِكَةٌ لَا يَعْلَمُ عِدَّتَهُمْ [in M and A: "عددهم" (their number)] إِلَّا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، يَعْبُدُونَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، عَلَى أَغْصَانِهَا، فِي كُلِّ مَوْضِعِ شَعْرَةٍ مِنْهَا مَلَكٌ. وَمَقَامُ جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فِي وَسَطِهَا، فَيُنَادِي اللَّهُ جِبْرِيلَ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةِ قَدْرٍ مَعَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ الَّذِينَ يَسْكُنُونَ سِدْرَةَ الْمُنْتَهَى، وَلَيْسَ فِيهِمْ مَلَكٌ إِلَّا قَدْ أُعْطِيَ الرَّأْفَةَ وَالرَّحْمَةَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ، فَيَنْزِلُونَ [in A: "مع" (with)] جِبْرِيلَ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ حِينَ تَغْرُبُ الشَّمْسُ، فَلَا تَبْقَى بُقْعَةٌ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ إِلَّا وَعَلَيْهَا مَلَكٌ، إِمَّا سَاجِدٌ وَإِمَّا قَائِمٌ، يَدْعُو لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ، إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ كَنِيسَةً أَوْ بِيعَةً، أَوْ بَيْتَ نَارٍ أَوْ وَثَنٍ، أَوْ بَعْضَ أَمَاكِنِكُمُ الَّتِي تَطْرَحُونَ فِيهَا الْخَبَثَ، أَوْ بَيْتًا فِيهِ سَكْرَانُ، أَوْ بَيْتًا فِيهِ مُسْكِرٌ، أَوْ بَيْتًا فِيهِ وَثَنٌ مَنْصُوبٌ، أَوْ بَيْتًا فِيهِ جَرَسٌ مُعَلَّقٌ، أَوْ مَبْوَلَةٌ، أَوْ مَكَانًا فِيهِ كَسَاحَةِ الْبَيْتِ، فَلَا يَزَالُونَ لَيْلَتَهُمْ تِلْكَ يَدْعُونَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ، وَجِبْرِيلُ لَا يَدَعُ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [in A: "من الناس" (of the people)] إِلَّا صَافَحَهُ، وَعَلَامَةُ ذَلِكَ أَنْ يَقْشَعِرَّ جِلْدُهُ، وَيَرِقَّ قَلْبُهُ، وَتَدْمَعَ عَيْنَاهُ، فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ مُصَافَحَةِ جِبْرِيلَ.

وَذَكَرَ كَعْبٌ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَالَ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: "لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ" ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِوَاحِدَةٍ، وَنَجَا مِنَ النَّارِ بِوَاحِدَةٍ، وَأَدْخَلَهُ الْجَنَّةَ بِوَاحِدَةٍ. فَقُلْنَا لِكَعْبِ الْأَحْبَارِ: يَا أَبَا إِسْحَاقَ، صَادِقًا؟ فَقَالَ كَعْبٌ: وَهَلْ يَقُولُ: "لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ" فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ إِلَّا كُلُّ صَادِقٍ؟ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، إِنَّ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ لَتَثْقُلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِ وَالْمُنَافِقِ، حَتَّى كَأَنَّ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ جَبَلًا، فَلَا تَزَالُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ هَكَذَا حَتَّى يَطْلُعَ الْفَجْرُ. فَأَوَّلُ مَنْ يَصْعَدُ جِبْرِيلُ، حَتَّى يَكُونَ فِي وَجْهِ الْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلَى مِنَ الشَّمْسِ، فَيَبْسُطُ جَنَاحَيْهِ، وَلَهُ جَنَاحَانِ أَخْضَرَانِ، لَا يَنْشُرُهُمَا إِلَّا فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ، فَتَصِيرُ الشَّمْسُ لَا شُعَاعَ لَهَا، ثُمَّ يَدْعُو مَلَكًا [in M: "ملكا ملكا" (one angel after another)] فَيَصْعَدُ، فَيَجْتَمِعُ نُورُ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَنُورُ جَنَاحَيْ جِبْرِيلَ، فَلَا تَزَالُ الشَّمْسُ يَوْمَهَا ذَلِكَ مُتَحَيِّرَةً، فَيُقِيمُ جِبْرِيلُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ بَيْنَ الْأَرْضِ وَبَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا يَوْمَهُمْ ذَلِكَ، فِي دُعَاءٍ وَرَحْمَةٍ وَاسْتِغْفَارٍ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ، وَلِمَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ احْتِسَابًا، وَدُعَاءٍ لِمَنْ حَدَّثَ نَفْسَهُ إِنْ عَاشَ إِلَى قَابِلٍ أَنْ يَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ لِلَّهِ. فَإِذَا أَمْسَوْا [in A: "فإذا استووا" (when they have leveled off)] دَخَلُوا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا، فَيَجْلِسُونَ حِلَقًا [حِلَقًا] [repeated word added from M]، فَتَجْتَمِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ مَلَائِكَةُ سَمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا، فَيَسْأَلُونَهُمْ عَنْ رَجُلٍ رَجُلٍ، وَعَنِ امْرَأَةٍ امْرَأَةٍ [in M: "عن رجل عن رجل وعن امرأة عن امرأة"]، فَيُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا: مَاذَا فَعَلَ فُلَانٌ؟ وَكَيْفَ وَجَدْتُمُوهُ الْعَامَ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: وَجَدْنَا فُلَانًا عَامَ أَوَّلَ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ مُتَعَبِّدًا، وَوَجَدْنَاهُ الْعَامَ مُبْتَدِعًا، وَوَجَدْنَا فُلَانًا مُبْتَدِعًا، وَوَجَدْنَاهُ الْعَامَ عَابِدًا. قَالَ: فَيَكُفُّونَ عَنِ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِذَلِكَ، وَيُقْبِلُونَ عَلَى الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِهَذَا، وَيَقُولُونَ: وَجَدْنَا فُلَانًا وَفُلَانًا يَذْكُرَانِ اللَّهَ، وَوَجَدْنَا فُلَانًا رَاكِعًا، وَفُلَانًا سَاجِدًا، وَوَجَدْنَاهُ تَالِيًا لِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ. قَالَ: فَهُمْ كَذَلِكَ يَوْمَهُمْ وَلَيْلَتَهُمْ، حَتَّى يَصْعَدُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الثَّانِيَةِ، فَفِي كُلِّ سَمَاءٍ يَوْمٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ، حَتَّى يَنْتَهُوا مَكَانَهُمْ مِنْ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى [in A: "في" (in)]، فَتَقُولُ لَهُمْ سِدْرَةُ الْمُنْتَهَى: يَا سُكَّانِي، حَدِّثُونِي عَنِ النَّاسِ وَسَمُّوهُمْ لِي، فَإِنَّ لِي عَلَيْكُمْ حَقًّا، وَإِنِّي أُحِبُّ مَنْ أَحَبَّ اللَّهَ. فَذَكَرَ كَعْبُ الْأَحْبَارِ أَنَّهُمْ يَعُدُّونَ لَهَا، وَيَحْكُونَ لَهَا الرَّجُلَ وَالْمَرْأَةَ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ وَأَسْمَاءِ آبَائِهِمْ. ثُمَّ تُقْبِلُ الْجَنَّةُ عَلَى السِّدْرَةِ فَتَقُولُ: أَخْبِرِينِي بِمَا أَخْبَرَكِ [in A: "بما أخبروك"] سُكَّانُكِ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ. فَتُخْبِرُهَا، قَالَ: فَتَقُولُ الْجَنَّةُ: رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى فُلَانٍ، وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى فُلَانَةَ، اللَّهُمَّ عَجِّلْهُمْ إِلَيَّ. فَيَبْلُغُ جِبْرِيلُ مَكَانَهَا قَبْلَهُمْ، فَيُلْهِمُهُ اللَّهُ فَيَقُولُ: وَجَدْتُ فُلَانًا سَاجِدًا فَاغْفِرْ لَهُ، فَيَغْفِرُ لَهُ، فَيَسْمَعُ جِبْرِيلُ جَمِيعَ حَمَلَةِ الْعَرْشِ فَيَقُولُونَ: رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى فُلَانٍ، وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى فُلَانَةَ، وَمَغْفِرَتُهُ لِفُلَانٍ [in M: "ومغفرة"]، وَيَقُولُ [in A: "ويقولون"] يَا رَبِّ، وَجَدْتُ عَبْدَكَ فُلَانًا الَّذِي وَجَدْتُهُ عَامَ أَوَّلَ عَلَى السُّنَّةِ وَالْعِبَادَةِ، وَوَجَدْتُهُ الْعَامَ قَدْ أَحْدَثَ حَدَثًا وَتَوَلَّى عَمَّا أُمِرَ بِهِ. فَيَقُولُ اللَّهُ: يَا جِبْرِيلُ، إِنْ تَابَ فَأَعْتَبَنِي قَبْلَ أَنْ يَمُوتَ بِثَلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ غَفَرْتُ لَهُ. فَيَقُولُ جِبْرِيلُ: لَكَ الْحَمْدُ إِلَهِي، أَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ خَلْقِكَ، وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ بِعِبَادِكَ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ. قَالَ: فَيَرْتَجُّ الْعَرْشُ وَمَا حَوْلَهُ، وَالْحُجُبُ وَالسَّمَوَاتُ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، تَقُولُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الرَّحِيمِ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الرَّحِيمِ.

قَالَ: وَذَكَرَ كَعْبٌ أَنَّهُ مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ وَهُوَ يُحَدِّثُ نَفْسَهُ إِذَا أَفْطَرَ بَعْدَ رَمَضَانَ أَلَّا يَعْصِيَ اللَّهَ، دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ بِغَيْرِ مَسْأَلَةٍ وَلَا حِسَابٍ.

آخِرُ تَفْسِيرِ سُورَةِ "لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ" [وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ وَالْمِنَّةُ] [addition from M].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 97, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 4):

Tafsir of Surat al-Qadr [In A: "Surat Laylat al-Qadr".]
It is Meccan.
In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
* *
Allah, exalted is He, informs that He sent down the Qur'an on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), which is the blessed night about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 3], and it is the Night of Power, and it is in the month of Ramadan, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].
Ibn 'Abbas and others said: Allah sent the Qur'an down all at once from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the House of Glory (Bayt al-'Izza) in the lowest heaven, and then it was sent down in parts, according to events, over twenty-three years upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then He, exalted is He, said, magnifying the status of the Night of Power, in which He singled out the sending down of the Great Qur'an: ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾.
Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi, when commenting on this verse, said: Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Abu Dawud at-Tayalisi narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Hudani [In A: "al-Judhami".] narrated to us from Yusuf ibn Sa'd, who said: A man stood up before al-Hasan ibn 'Ali after he had pledged allegiance to Mu'awiyah and said: "You have blackened the faces of the believers" – or: "O you who blacken the faces of the believers" – so he said: "Do not reproach me, may Allah have mercy on you; the Prophet ﷺ was shown the Banu Umayyah on his pulpit, and that grieved him, so there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ – O Muhammad – meaning a river in Paradise – and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power. And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – the Banu Umayyah will rule it after you, O Muhammad." Al-Qasim said: "We counted, and it came to a thousand months, not exceeding a day or falling short by a day." [Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3350).]
Then at-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith, which we only know from this route, through the hadith of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, and he is trustworthy; Yahya al-Qattan and Ibn Mahdi declared him trustworthy. He said: His teacher Yusuf ibn Sa'd – and it is said: Yusuf ibn Mazin – is an unknown man, and we do not know this hadith in this wording except through this route.
This hadith was also narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, from Yusuf ibn Mazin, with the same [Al-Mustadrak (3/170), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il an-Nubuwwah (6/509).] . Al-Tirmidhi's statement that this Yusuf is unknown is open to question, for a group narrated from him, among them Hammad ibn Salamah, Khalid al-Hadhdha', and Yunus ibn 'Ubayd. Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "He is well known," and in a report from Ibn Ma'in [he said]: "He is trustworthy." [Addition from M.] Ibn Jarir narrated it through the route of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, from 'Isa ibn Mazin, so he said, and this implies confusion (idtirab) in this hadith, and Allah knows best. Then this hadith, in every case, is extremely munkar (rejected). Our shaykh, the Imam, the Hafiz, the Proof Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: "It is a munkar hadith."
I say: The statement of al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl al-Hudani [In A: "al-Judhami".] that he calculated the period of the Banu Umayyah and found it to be a thousand months, not exceeding a day or falling short by a day, is not correct. Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him, became sole ruler when al-Hasan ibn 'Ali handed over the command to him in the year forty (AH), and the allegiance was unified for Mu'awiyah, and that year was called the Year of Unity (ʿAm al-Jama'a). Then they continued in it consecutively in al-Sham and elsewhere; it was not taken from them except during the rule of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr in the two Sanctuaries, al-Ahwaz and some regions, for nearly nine years, but their hand was not wholly removed from command, only from some regions, until the 'Abbasids seized the caliphate from them in the year one hundred and thirty-two (AH). So the total of their period is ninety-two years, and that is more than a thousand months, for a thousand months is equivalent to eighty-three years and four months. It seems al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl dropped from their period the days of Ibn al-Zubayr, and on this basis what he said is close to correct in calculation, and Allah knows best.
Among what indicates the weakness of this hadith is that it is framed to disparage the rule of the Banu Umayyah, and if that were intended it would not have been in this context; for the excellence of the Night of Power over their days does not indicate the blame of their days, since the Night of Power is very noble, and the noble surah came only to praise the Night of Power. How then would it be praised by being preferred over the days of the Banu Umayyah, which, by the implication of this hadith, are blameworthy? Is this not like what the poet said:
Do you not see that the sword's worth diminishes
when it is said that the sword is more effective than the staff?
And another said:
When you prefer a man of skill
over one deficient, the praise becomes a deficiency.
Then what is understood from the Qur'an's reference to the thousand months mentioned in the verse [In M: "Then what is understood from the verse that".] is the days of the Banu Umayyah, while the surah is Meccan, so how can it refer to a thousand months being the rule of the Banu Umayyah, when neither the wording nor the meaning of the verse indicates it?! The pulpit was made in Madinah only after a period from the Hijrah. All of this indicates the weakness and rejection of this hadith, and Allah knows best. [And see: al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (6/243, 244), for he also expanded on the discussion of this hadith.]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Muslim – meaning Ibn Khalid – informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: The Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who wore weapons in the path of Allah for a thousand months. He said: The Muslims marvelled at that. He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power. And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – the night in which that man wore weapons in the path of Allah for a thousand months. [Al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, as in the takhrij of al-Zayla'i's Takhrij al-Kashshaf (4/253), narrated it through the route of Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with it as a mursal report.]
Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Mujahid, who said: There was a man among the Children of Israel who would stand in prayer at night until morning, then strive against the enemy by day until evening, and he did this for a thousand months, so Allah revealed this verse: ﴿The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – the standing in prayer on that night is better than that man's deeds. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/167).]
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Maslamah ibn 'Ali narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn 'Urwah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ once mentioned four men from the Children of Israel who worshipped Allah for eighty years without disobeying Him for the blink of an eye: he mentioned Ayyub, Zakariyya, Hizqil ibn al-'Ajuz, and Yusha' ibn Nun. He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marvelled at that, so Jibril came to him and said: "O Muhammad, your Ummah marvels at the worship of these men for eighty years without disobeying Him for the blink of an eye; Allah has sent down something better than that." Then he recited to him: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Power. And what will make you know what the Night of Power is? The Night of Power is better than a thousand months﴾ – this is better than what you and your Ummah marvelled at. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delighted by that, and so were the people with him. [And al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/569) and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim.]
Sufyan al-Thawri said: It reached me from Mujahid: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." He said: Its deeds – its fasting and its standing in prayer – are better than a thousand months. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months" – the Night of Power is not among those months. Qatadah ibn Di'amah, al-Shafi'i, and others besides them said likewise.
'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i said: Deeds performed in it are better than the deeds of a thousand months.
This view, that it is better than worship of a thousand months – and that the Night of Power is not among them – is the choice of Ibn Jarir. It is the correct view and not what differs from it, and it is like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "A night of guarding (ribat) in the path of Allah is better than a thousand nights elsewhere in other stations." Narrated by Ahmad [Al-Musnad (1/62), from the hadith of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him.] And like what has come concerning one who goes to the Friday prayer with good bearing and a good intention: "It is written for him the reward of a year's deeds, the reward of its fasting and its standing in prayer," and other meanings similar to these.
Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When Ramadan arrived, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The month of Ramadan has come to you, a blessed month. Allah has made its fasting obligatory upon you. The gates of Paradise are opened in it, the gates of Hellfire are closed in it, and the devils are chained in it. In it is a night better than a thousand months; whoever is deprived of its good has indeed been deprived."
An-Nasa'i also narrated it through the hadith of Ayyub, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (2/230) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (4/129).]
Since the worship on the Night of Power equals the worship of a thousand months, it is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Power in faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1901) and Sahih Muslim no. (760).]
* *
His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾ means: the angels descend in abundance on this night because of the abundance of its blessing, and the angels descend along with the descent of blessing and mercy, just as they descend at the recitation of the Qur'an, surround the circles of remembrance, and lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge out of sincere reverence for him.
As for the Spirit, it has been said that what is meant here is Jibril, peace be upon him, so it is of the type of mentioning the specific after the general. It has also been said that they are a kind of angel, as was mentioned earlier in Surat an-Naba'. And Allah knows best.
* *
His saying: ﴿concerning every matter﴾ – Mujahid said: "Peace is it, concerning every matter."
Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Peace is it﴾, he said: "It is safe; Satan cannot do any evil in it or cause any harm in it."
Qatadah and others said: Matters are decided therein, and lifespans and provisions are determined, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Therein every wise matter is distinguished﴾.
* *
His saying: ﴿Peace it is until the rising of the dawn﴾. Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿concerning every matter, peace it is until the rising of the dawn﴾, he said: "It is the greeting of the angels on the Night of Power to the people of the mosques, until dawn rises."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: "Min kulli imri'in salamun hiya hatta matli'i al-fajr" (from every person, peace it is until the rising of the dawn).

Al-Bayhaqi, in his book Fada'il al-Awqat, narrated from 'Ali a strange report about the descent of the angels, their passing by those who pray on the Night of Power, and the attainment of blessing by those who pray.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar a very strange and wondrous, extremely lengthy report about the descent of the angels from Sidrat al-Muntaha in the company of Jibril, peace be upon him, to the earth, and their supplication for the believing men and women. [The report will be cited at the explanation of the end of the surah.]

Ibn Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Imran (i.e., al-Qattan) narrated to us from Qatadah, from Abu Maymunah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the Night of Decree: "It is a night of the twenty-seventh or the twenty-ninth, and the angels on that night on the earth are more numerous than the pebbles" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2545).]].

al-A'mash said, from al-Minhal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, regarding His words ﴿Peace it is, until the emergence of dawn﴾: "No matter is decreed in it."

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿Peace it is﴾, meaning: "It is entirely good; there is no evil in it until the rising of dawn." This meaning is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Haywah [[In A: "Abdah".]] ibn Shurayh narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us: Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Night of Decree is in the last ten nights. Whoever stands in prayer during them, seeking its reward, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sins and what followed. It is an odd night: the ninth, the seventh, the fifth, the third, or the last night." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: "The sign of the Night of Decree is that it is clear and bright, as if there were a shining moon in it, still and calm, neither cold nor hot, and no shooting star is permitted to be thrown on that night until morning. Its sign is that the sun rises in the morning level, without rays like the moon on the night of the full moon, and the Shaytan is not permitted to come out with it that day" [[Al-Musnad (5/324).]].

This chain is good (hasan), but the text has strangeness (gharabah), and some of its wording is objectionable (nakarah).

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Zam'ah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding the Night of Decree: "It is a gentle, open night, neither hot nor cold, and the sun of its morning rises weak and red" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2680), in which it reads "safiqah" instead of "ḍa'ifah".]].

Ibn Abi Asim al-Nabil narrated with his chain from Jabir ibn Abd Allah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw the Night of Decree and then I was made to forget it. It is in the last ten nights. Among its nights is a clear, bright night, neither hot nor cold, as if there were a moon in it. Its Shaytan does not come out until its dawn breaks" [[Al-Kanz (8/540), no. (24069), attributed it to him, but I have not found it in the Sunnah. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2190), through Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, in similar wording.]].

**Section**

The scholars differed: was the Night of Decree in earlier nations, or is it specific to this Ummah? There are two opinions.

Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri said: Malik narrated to us that it reached him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shown the lifespans of people before him, or what Allah willed of that, and it seemed that the lifespans of his Ummah were too short for them to reach the same amount of deeds that others reached in long life. So Allah gave him the Night of Decree, which is better than a thousand months [[Al-Muwatta' in the narration of al-Zuhri, no. (889).]]. It has also been traced through another chain.

What Malik said implies that this Ummah is specifically given the Night of Decree. The author of "al-Uddah," one of the imams of the Shafi'is, transmitted this from the majority of scholars, and Allah knows best. Al-Khattabi reported a consensus (ijma') on it, and al-Rafi'i stated it definitively as the position of the school (madhhab). What the hadith indicates is that it existed in the earlier nations as it does in our Ummah.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar: Abu Zumayl Simak al-Hanafi narrated to me: Malik ibn Murthid ibn Abd Allah narrated to me: Murthid narrated to me, saying: I asked Abu Dharr: "How did you ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Night of Decree?" He said: "I used to ask people about it. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me about the Night of Decree: is it in Ramadan or in another month?' He said: 'Rather, it is in Ramadan.' I said: 'Does it remain with the prophets as long as they are alive, and when they die it is lifted?' He said: 'Rather, it remains until the Day of Resurrection.' I said: 'In which Ramadan is it?' He said: 'Seek it in the first ten and the last ten.'" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke and kept talking, then I seized his moment of distraction and said: "In which of the two tens is it?" He said: "Seek it in the last ten nights; do not ask me about anything after that." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke again, then I seized his moment of distraction and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I adjure you by my right over you, tell me in which ten it is." He became angry with me with an anger the like of which he had not shown since I accompanied him, and said: "Seek it in the last seven nights; do not ask me about anything after that."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from al-Fallas, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, with it [[Al-Musnad (5/171) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (3427).]].

In it is evidence for what we mentioned, and in it is that it continues until the Day of Resurrection, every year [after the Prophet ﷺ] [[Addition from A.]]. This is not as some sects of the Shi'ah claimed, that it was lifted entirely, based on their understanding of the hadith we will mention below, in his words, peace be upon him: "It was lifted, and perhaps that is better for you," because what is meant is the lifting of knowledge of its exact time. It also indicates that the Night of Decree is specifically tied to the month of Ramadan among all other months, not as was reported from Ibn Mas'ud and those who followed him among the scholars of Kufa, that it can be found in all of the year and is hoped for equally in all months.

Abu Dawud in his Sunan titled a chapter on this: "Chapter on clarifying that the Night of Decree is in every Ramadan." He narrated: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh al-Nasa'i [[In M: "al-Shami".]] informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us: Musa ibn Uqbah narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked, while I was listening, about the Night of Decree, and he said: "It is in every Ramadan" [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1387).]].

This chain's narrators are trustworthy (thiqah), except that Abu Dawud said: Shu'bah and Sufyan narrated it from Abu Ishaq, and they stopped it (at Ibn Umar, as a statement, not a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ).

It has been reported from Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, a narration that it is hoped for throughout the whole month of Ramadan. This is an opinion (wajh) transmitted by al-Ghazali, and al-Rafi'i considered it very strange.

**Section**

Then it has been said: it is on the first night of the month of Ramadan, reported from Abu Razin. It has also been said: it falls on the night of the seventeenth. Abu Dawud narrated a hadith on this from Ibn Mas'ud, traced to the Prophet ﷺ, and it is also reported as a statement (mawquf) attributed to him, and to Zayd ibn Arqam and Uthman ibn Abi al-As.

This is an opinion from Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, and it is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri. They justified it by saying that it is the night of Badr. It was a Friday night, the seventeenth of Ramadan, and in its morning was the Battle of Badr, the day of which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿the Day of Criterion﴾ [Al-Anfal: 41].

It has been said: the nineteenth night, reported also from Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both.

It has been said: the twenty-first night, based on the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ secluded himself (i'tikaf) in the first ten days of Ramadan, and we secluded ourselves with him. Then Jibril came to him and said: "What you seek is ahead of you." So he secluded himself in the middle ten, and we secluded ourselves with him. Then Jibril came to him and said: "[What] you seek is ahead of you [[Addition from M and A.]]." Then the Prophet ﷺ stood up delivering a sermon on the morning of the twentieth of Ramadan, and said: "Whoever was secluded with me should return, for I was shown the Night of Decree, and I was made to forget it. It is in the last ten nights, in odd nights. I saw myself prostrating in mud and water." The roof of the mosque was made of palm fronds, and we did not see anything in the sky, but then a cloud came and it rained, and the Prophet ﷺ led us in prayer until I saw the trace of mud and water on the forehead of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, confirming his vision. In another wording: "In the morning of the twenty-first." They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1167).]].

al-Shafi'i said: This hadith is the most authentic of the reports.

It has been said: the twenty-third night, based on the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Unays in Sahih Muslim [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1168).]], which is close in context to the narration of Abu Sa'id. Allah knows best.

It has been said: the twenty-fourth night. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-fourth." Its chain's narrators are trustworthy [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2167).]].

Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from al-Sunabihi, from Bilal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Night of Decree is the night of the twenty-fourth" [[Al-Musnad (6/12).]].

Ibn Lahi'ah is weak (da'if). What contradicts him is what al-Bukhari narrated from Asbagh, from Ibn Wahb, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Abu Abd Allah al-Sunabihi, who said: Bilal, the muezzin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, informed me that it is the first of the seven nights of the last ten. So this statement traced to a companion is more authentic, and Allah knows best. Similarly it has been reported from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abd Allah ibn Wahb that it is the night of the twenty-fourth. It has already been mentioned in the commentary of Surah al-Baqarah [[At the commentary of verse 185.]] the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' traced to the Prophet ﷺ: "The Qur'an was sent down on the night of the twenty-fourth."

It has been said: it is the night of the twenty-fifth, based on what al-Bukhari narrated from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek it in the last ten nights of Ramadan, on the ninth remaining, on the seventh remaining, on the fifth remaining." Many scholars interpreted this as the odd nights, which is more apparent and more well-known. Others understood it as the even nights, as narrated by Muslim from Abu Sa'id, who interpreted it that way. Allah knows best.

It has been said: it is the night of the twenty-seventh, based on what Muslim narrated in his Sahih from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "It is the night of the twenty-seventh."

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us: I heard Abdah and Asim, from Zirr: I asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b, "Abu al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Mas'ud says: 'Whoever stands in prayer throughout the year will find the Night of Decree.'" He said: "May Allah have mercy on him. He knew that it is in the month of Ramadan, and that it is the night of the twenty-seventh." Then he swore an oath. I said: "How do you know that?" He said: "By the sign, or the verse, that he told us of: the sun rises on that day without rays." Referring to the sun [[Al-Musnad (5/130).]].

And Muslim narrated it through the chains of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, Shu'ba and al-Awza'i, from 'Abda, from Zirr, from Ubayy, and he mentioned it, and in it he said: "By Allah, other than whom there is no god, it is in Ramadan," (he swore without making an exception), "By Allah, I know which night is the Night of Decree, the one the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to stand in prayer during. It is the night of the twenty-seventh, and its sign is that the sun rises on its morning white, without rays." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (762).]]

There are also reports on this from Mu'awiya, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas and others [[See these and other hadiths in al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti (8/570-580).]], from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that it is the night of the twenty-seventh. This is the view of a group of the early scholars (al-salaf), and it is the well-trodden path (al-jadda) of the school of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is also a narration from Abu Hanifa. It has been related from some of the early scholars that he tried to derive that it is the night of the twenty-seventh from the Qur'an, from the words ﴿It [is]﴾, because it is the twenty-seventh word of the surah. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari related to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada and 'Asim, that they both heard 'Ikrima say: Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab summoned the companions of Muhammad [[In A: "companions of the Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ and asked them about the Night of Decree, and they agreed that it is in the last ten nights. Ibn 'Abbas said: I said to 'Umar: "I know, or I think, which night of the Night of Decree it is." 'Umar said: "Which night is it?" [I said] [[Addition from M and A.]] "The seventh that passes, or the seventh that remains, of the last ten nights." 'Umar said: "How did you know that?" Ibn 'Abbas said: I said: "Allah created seven heavens, seven earths and seven days; the month revolves around seven; man was created from seven; he eats from seven; he prostrates on seven; the circumambulation of the House is seven; the stoning of the pillars is seven..." for things he mentioned. 'Umar said: "You have indeed understood a matter that we did not understand." Qatada would add to Ibn 'Abbas's statement "and he eats from seven" that it refers to the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then We caused to grow therein grain, and grapes and herbs [[Addition from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/322).]] ...﴾ [Abasa: 27, 28] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/322).]].

This is a good chain (isnad, the chain of narrators), strong, but its wording (matn) is very unusual.

It has also been said that it occurs on the night of the twenty-ninth. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, related to us, Sa'id ibn Salama related to us, 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil related to us, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Night of Decree, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Ramadan. So seek it in the last ten nights, for it is on an odd night: the twenty-first, or the twenty-third, or the twenty-fifth, or the twenty-seventh, [or the twenty-ninth] [[Addition from A and al-Musnad.]], or on the last night." [[Al-Musnad (5/321).]]

Al-Imam Ahmad also said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, that is Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, related to us, 'Imran al-Qattan related to us, from Qatada, from Abu Maymuna [[In A: "from Abu Mu'awiya".]], from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about the Night of Decree: "It is the seventh or the ninth and twentieth night, and the angels on that night on the earth are more numerous than the number of pebbles." [[Al-Musnad (2/519).]]

Only Ahmad related this, and its chain is acceptable (la ba'sa bihi).

It has also been said that it occurs on the last night, due to what preceded in this hadith just now [[In A: "also".]], and due to what al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i related, from the hadith of 'Uyayna ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Bakra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In the nine remaining, or the seven remaining, or the five remaining, or the three, or the last night." He meant: seek the Night of Decree. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (794) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (3404).]]

Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih. In the Musnad, through the chain of Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the Night of Decree: "It is the last night." [[I have not found it in the Musnad, but al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/572) and attributed it to Ahmad. Perhaps I will add it later.]]

Section

Al-Shafi'i [al-Imam] [[Addition from A.]] said regarding these narrations: They were issued by the Prophet ﷺ as an answer to the questioner, when it was said to him: "Shall I seek the Night of Decree on such-and-such night?" and he would say: "Yes." The Night of Decree is only a specific night that does not shift. This was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi from him in meaning. And it is related from Abu Qilaba that he said: "The Night of Decree shifts within the last ten nights."

What he related from Abu Qilaba was explicitly stated by Malik, al-Thawri, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu Thawr, al-Muzani, Abu Bakr ibn Khuzayma and others. It is also attributed to al-Shafi'i, as transmitted by al-Qadi from him, and it is the more likely view. And Allah knows best.

This view may find some support in what is established in the two Sahihs, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: that some men from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ were shown the Night of Decree in dreams in the last seven nights of Ramadan, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I see that your dreams agree on the last seven nights, so whoever seeks it, let him seek it in the last seven nights." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2015) and Sahih Muslim no. (1165).]]

Also in them, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Seek the Night of Decree on the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2017) and Sahih Muslim no. (1169). The wording is that of al-Bukhari.]]

Al-Shafi'i's position that it does not shift and is fixed within the month is argued from what al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to inform us of the Night of Decree, but two men among the Muslims quarrelled, and he said: "I went out to inform you of the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, so it was lifted. Perhaps that is better for you. So seek it on the ninth, the seventh and the fifth." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2023).]]

The point of evidence from it: if it were not fixed and continuously specified, they would not have come to know its specific night every year, since if it shifted they would only have known its specific night in that one year. Unless it is said that he went out only to inform them of it that year.

* *

His saying "so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, so it was lifted": in it there is support for what is said, that disputation cuts off benefit and beneficial knowledge, as came in the hadith: "Indeed a servant is deprived of provision through a sin that befalls him."

* *

His saying "it was lifted" means that the knowledge of its specific identity was lifted from you, not that it was lifted entirely from existence, as the ignorant among the Shi'a say, because he said after this: "So seek it on the ninth, the seventh and the fifth."

* *

His saying "Perhaps that is better for you" means: its not being specified for you, for when it is undetermined, those seeking it strive to find it in all the places where it is hoped for, and this produces more worship. This is unlike when they know its specific night, for then their resolve would be limited to standing in prayer on it alone. The wisdom required its being undetermined so that worship would encompass the whole month in seeking it, and the striving would be greater in the last ten nights. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) in the last ten nights of Ramadan until Allah took him, Mighty and Majestic is He. Then his wives observed i'tikaf after him. Both of them [al-Bukhari and Muslim] related it from the hadith of 'A'isha. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2026) and Sahih Muslim no. (1172).]]

And they both have from Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to observe i'tikaf in the last ten nights of Ramadan. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2025) and Sahih Muslim no. (1171).]]

'A'isha said: When the last ten nights began, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend the night in worship, wake his family, and tighten his waist-wrap (shadd al-mi'zar). Both of them related it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2024) and Sahih Muslim no. (1174).]]

Muslim has from her [[In M: "from both of them".]]: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would strive in the ten nights more than he strove at any other time. [[Sahih Muslim no. (1175).]]

This is the meaning of her words "and tightened the waist-wrap." It has been said that what is meant by it is abstaining from women. It may be that it is a metaphor for both matters, based on what Imam Ahmad related:

Suraij related to us, Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, who said: When ten nights of Ramadan remained, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would tighten his waist-wrap and withdraw from his wives. Ahmad alone related it. [[Al-Musnad (6/66).]]

It has been related from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, that all the nights of the last ten are equal in seeking the Night of Decree, and no one night is preferred over another. I saw this in the Sharh of al-Rafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

The recommended course is to increase supplication at all times, more in Ramadan, more in its last ten nights, and more on its odd nights. It is recommended to repeatedly say: "O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me," because of what Imam Ahmad related:

Yazid, that is Ibn Harun, related to us, al-Jurayri [[In M: "al-Jawhari".]], that is Sa'id ibn Iyas, related to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Buraida, that 'A'isha said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I happen to coincide with the Night of Decree, what should I supplicate?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me." [[Al-Musnad (6/182).]]

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Maja, through the chain of Kahmas ibn al-Hasan, from 'Abdullah ibn Buraida, from 'A'isha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if I know which night is the Night of Decree, what should I say in it?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3513), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11688) and Sunan Ibn Maja no. (3850).]]

This is the wording of al-Tirmidhi, then he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Hakim also related it in his Mustadrak and said: "This is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs." [[Al-Mustadrak (1/531).]] Al-Nasa'i also related it through the chain of Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Alqama ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraida, from 'A'isha, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if I coincide with the Night of Decree, what should I say in it?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and love pardon, so pardon me." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10713).]]

A strange report and a wondrous account is mentioned, connected to the Night of Decree, which Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim related when interpreting this noble surah, and he said:
